beliefs: Trailing whitespace is stripped, including Unicode whitespace like NBSP and em-space [E1, E2, E5]
Leading whitespace is preserved, so '  hello' stays '  hello' [E2, E3]
After stripping, the first character is title-cased only if it is at position 0 of the original string; if the string starts with whitespace, nothing is uppercased [E3, E7]
The first character uses title-case semantics (.title() on that char), so 'ß'→'Ss', 'ﬁ'→'Fi', 'ﬃ'→'Ffi', 'ŉ'→'ʼN', 'ǆ'→'ǅ' [E5, E6, E7, E8, E9]
The remainder of the string after the first character is lowercased, so 'ÉCOLE'→'École', 'Hello WORLD'→'Hello world', 'A1B2C!'→'A1b2c!' [E11]
A lone space or all-space string becomes empty after trailing-strip [E1, E2]
A tab or newline at position 0 is not uppercased and is preserved [E2, E3]
Digits, symbols, and already-uppercase letters at position 0 are unchanged [E1, E4]
